subject: Set random-number seed for calls to obj$simulate()

messages.author: e7a8779ef7a944e5
messages.subject: Set random-number seed for calls to obj$simulate()
parts:
Hi all,

I'm using the SIMULATE feature in TMB as accessed in R via obj$simulate() to implement a simulator in R package VAST.  In some cases, its helpful to exactly replicate a simulation experiment by passing the same random-number seed; however, I don't see how to do this using the obj$simulate() feature.

Is there any way to pass a random-number seed, either in TMB code when calling SIMULATE or (ideally) by passing a seed to obj$simulate() on the R side?

Thanks 
Jim

in TMB:

   SIMULATE {
   y = rnorm(mu, sigma);
   REPORT(y);
}


// In R
obj =  MakeADFun(data = data, parameters=pars,..........)  
obj$simulate()$y

messages.author: 55d0e2f87b0f795e
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Set random-number seed for calls to obj$simulate()
parts:
Hi Jim,

You could look at simulate.glmmTMB() for an example (sorry if it’s more complicated than necessary). 
https://github.com/glmmTMB/glmmTMB/blob/master/glmmTMB/R/methods.R#L1057

object$obj$simulate() is just taking it from set.seed() but simulate.glmmTMB() is written so that it can take the seed from either the function call (and later restore the RNG state (R.seed in the example code) that was in the environment before calling simulate.glmmTMB()), or take the seed from the environment. E.g. s2 and s3 give the same numbers in the example below, but the call to s3 maintains the RNG state that was already in the environment.

data(cbpp, package="lme4")
(bovine <- glmmTMB(cbind(incidence, size-incidence) ~ period + (1|herd),
   family=binomial, data=cbpp))

set.seed(111); s2 <- simulate(bovine)
s3 <- simulate(bovine, seed=111)

Cheers,
Mollie
